clue.text: Infant being looked after for no great cost

definitions.meaning: a little child in someone's care, a young ward

explanation.surface: A baby is minded for a very reasonable fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A child minded by an adult is a little ward, while a low fee is a minor price; one phrase covers both senses.

clue.text: A square one should go round easily enough!

definitions.text: A square one should go round easily enough!

parts.words: A square one should go round easily enough!
parts.note: a hearty, substantial dinner is called square, and a generous serving is expected to feed everyone, despite the geometry joke of a square going round

explanation.surface: A geometry puzzle about fitting a square shape round something.
explanation.definitionFit: A square one is the idiom for a full, nourishing helping of food, ample enough to share around.

clue.text: Crude oil thus refined

indicators.note: refined oil has been processed and changed, so these letters are reworked into a new order

explanation.surface: A remark on crude oil being processed at a refinery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' looks like an adjective for the oil, but it is the definition; 'refined' rearranges OIL THUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude manners are boorish and coarse, like those of a yob.

clue.text: Common complaint caught by the elderly

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught
the old is a collective term for elderly people

explanation.surface: A remark that older people often catch a familiar ailment.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniffly head infection is the most ordinary ailment there is.

clue.text: Shocking in respect to certain individuals

parts.note: awe is deep reverential respect
some means certain unspecified people

explanation.surface: A phrase saying some particular people find something shocking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' and 'to' are links; the answer is used in its old sense of fearsome or dreadful.
explanation.definitionFit: In its older sense the word means dreadful, inspiring fear or dread, which is close to appalling.

clue.text: They give support to those that get burnt

definitions.meaning: ropes or cables steadying a tent or mast
effigies of Fawkes thrown on bonfires each 5 November in Britain

explanation.surface: A line about supporters of people who have been burnt.
explanation.walkthrough: On Bonfire Night (5 November) British children burn a stuffed effigy of Guy Fawkes.
explanation.definitionFit: Tent ropes brace a structure, and Bonfire Night effigies of Fawkes are burnt, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Spokesman?

parts.note: read not as a person speaking for others but as a craftsman who makes spokes for cartwheels

explanation.surface: A one-word query about who speaks for a group.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional craftsman who builds and repairs wooden wheels, fitting their spokes.

clue.text: Navy man and journalist

parts.note: a seventeenth-century naval administrator famous for keeping a diary, so a keeper of a journal

explanation.surface: A description of a sailor who also writes for a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'journalist' means one who keeps a journal: he was Secretary to the Admiralty and kept a celebrated diary of 1660s London.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous diarist worked as an Admiralty official, so he was both a naval official and a keeper of a daily journal.

clue.text: Version of carol Silent Night is heard

definitions.note: said aloud, night sounds like knight, a man given a title, as in Arthur's Round Table

indicators.note: a version of something is a reworking of it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A performance of the Christmas carol Silent Night can be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is itself a sound pun: 'Night is heard' gives knight, a knight of Arthur's Round Table; 'Version of' rearranges CAROL SILENT.
explanation.definitionFit: The best-known knight of the Round Table, Arthur's champion.

clue.text: The Greeks probably regarded it as a capital investment

definitions.text: The Greeks probably regarded it as a capital investment

parts.words: The Greeks probably regarded it as a capital investment
parts.note: investment in its military sense means besieging, and the capital is a city, so this is a ten-year blockade of a city by Greek armies

explanation.surface: A financial remark that ancient Greeks thought something an excellent investment.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary ten-year Greek blockade of Priam's city was the military encircling of a capital.

clue.text: Parliament or the Church makes men twisters

indicators.note: the letters of the following words are made into something new, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A jibe that politics or religion turns men into twisters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'makes' tells you to rearrange MEN TWISTERS; 'twisters' looks like the signal but is fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The London district names both the Houses of Parliament and the great Abbey and Cathedral there.

clue.text: Not a sunny greeting?

parts.note: a word for a salutation that is also icy precipitation, hardly sunny weather

explanation.surface: A query about an unfriendly hello.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a call of welcome and pellets of ice falling from clouds, which is no sunshine.

clue.text: Team with an air of superiority

definitions.meaning: pretentious, haughty manner, as in putting on airs

explanation.surface: A squad that comes across as arrogant.
explanation.definitionFit: A playing squad is one meaning, and haughty pretension is the other, as in having no airs.

clue.text: A heavenly intervention?

parts.note: not a divine act but one body in the sky coming between the sun and an observer

explanation.surface: A suggestion of a miracle from above.
explanation.definitionFit: When the moon passes in front of the sun, a celestial body literally intervenes and blocks its light.

clue.text: Ten dollars for a bird

definitions.meaning: a former United States gold coin worth ten dollars

explanation.surface: A price paid for a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The old American ten-dollar gold coin bore this name.
explanation.definitionFit: The American gold coin worth ten dollars shared its name with the raptor on the national emblem.

clue.text: Tom's nag is mixed in with others

indicators.note: mixed up letters are rearranged, so the letters before are reshuffled

parts.note: the name with its apostrophe dropped gives four letters

explanation.surface: A horse belonging to Tom is put in a field with other horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mixed' rearranges TOMS NAG; 'in with others' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Being among a group means mingled with its members, in their midst.

clue.text: Giant book of maps

definitions.meaning: the Titan of Greek myth who held up the sky

explanation.surface: A huge volume of charts.
explanation.definitionFit: The Titan who bore the heavens gave his name to map collections, which once showed him on their covers.

clue.text: Expedition has only half a tent

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: only half of the next word is kept, its first two letters

explanation.surface: A camping trip whose tent is only half there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expedition' here means speed, not a journey.
explanation.definitionFit: Expedition can mean promptness or speed of action, a synonym of hurry.

clue.text: Tighten the spring — it's a means of propulsion

definitions.meaning: to coil a clock or watch spring by turning its key
moving air that drives sailing ships and windmills

explanation.surface: Instructions to tension a spring that powers a device.
explanation.walkthrough: The held grid letters read WINO, an OCR slip; both senses give WIND, one verb and one noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Coiling a clockwork mechanism is to turn it up, and moving air pushes sails along, two senses of one word.

clue.text: Coil unwinds in places

indicators.note: a coil that unwinds loses its order, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A coil comes loose in spots.
explanation.definitionFit: Locations or positions, the Latin plural used in mathematics and genetics.

clue.text: A man fore-armed has such a nerve

definitions.text: A man fore-armed has such a nerve

parts.words: A man fore-armed has such a nerve
parts.note: plays on forewarned is forearmed: every forearm carries a particular nerve running along a bone

explanation.surface: A forearmed man shows real nerve.
explanation.walkthrough: The nerve running down the forearm along one of its two bones gives the funny bone its tingle.
explanation.definitionFit: The nerve named after a forearm bone runs along the little-finger side of the arm.

clue.text: Futile advice to the wasteful

definitions.meaning: read as two words, a recommendation to consume a smaller amount

explanation.surface: A remark that advising spendthrifts is pointless.
explanation.definitionFit: Pointless efforts are in vain, and split in two the word tells a squanderer to consume a smaller amount.

clue.text: One object in rent is investment

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the next, signalling a container

parts.note: an aim is an object or goal

explanation.surface: A landlord's note on something put into the rent as an investment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'investment' means clothing (what one is invested with), not money.
explanation.definitionFit: Investment in the old sense is clothing, as is attire or garments.

clue.text: I seem somehow to follow it in detail

indicators.note: the reshuffled letters come after the word it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: somehow means in some unknown way, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A speaker explains that they seem to grasp something in detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'somehow' rearranges I SEEM to EMISE, which 'to follow' places after IT; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To detail is to list point by point, setting out each element separately.

clue.text: A tussle for military honours

indicators.note: here signals the letters are exchanged for a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A scuffle over who gets decorations.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal is weak: 'for' asks for A TUSSLE to be exchanged for its rearrangement; a tussle itself suggests the jumbling.
explanation.definitionFit: Soldiers' raised-hand greetings and gun volleys are formal marks of respect in the forces.

clue.text: American gangster after Robin

definitions.meaning: US slang for a hoodlum or thug
the outlaw of Sherwood Forest, whose surname follows his first name

explanation.surface: A US mobster pursuing someone named Robin.
explanation.walkthrough: Robin ___ is the English outlaw of Sherwood Forest legend.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for hoodlum, it is American slang for a mobster, and it completes the outlaw's name.

clue.text: Piece of boarded adornment

indicators.note: a piece of the words is taken, so the answer is a run of letters within them

explanation.surface: A section of wall decoration made of boards.
explanation.walkthrough: The run straddles the two words, the last letter of 'boarded' and the start of 'adornment'.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden panelled band along the lower part of a wall is ornamental boarding.

clue.text: The hollow sound of success in business

definitions.meaning: a period of rapid commercial growth

explanation.surface: Commercial success has a hollow ring to it.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep resonant noise is one sense, and a surge in trade is the other.

clue.text: It's shouted as a warning, of course

definitions.text: It's shouted as a warning, of course

parts.words: It's shouted as a warning, of course
parts.note: of course looks like a mere aside but means on a golf course, where players call out ... driving

explanation.surface: Naturally, someone yells to alert others.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers call out this cry to alert people ahead that a ball is coming.

clue.text: Return of service takes love game

indicators.note: a return goes back the way it came, so the word for service is read backwards

parts.note: RAF, the Royal Air Force, is one of the armed services
love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

explanation.surface: A tennis rally: a return of serve wins a love game.
explanation.walkthrough: Tennis words throughout mislead: 'service' is a branch of the armed forces and 'love' is nil.
explanation.definitionFit: An old gambling card game played against a banker.

clue.text: Return from work at the end of the week?

definitions.text: Return from work at the end of the week?

parts.words: Return from work at the end of the week?
parts.note: return means earnings rather than going home, so this is the wage packet after deductions

explanation.surface: Going home from the job on Friday.
explanation.definitionFit: Net wages after tax are the reward one carries away from a job, often paid weekly.

clue.text: Complaint of the motorist using too much petrol?

definitions.text: Complaint of the motorist using too much petrol?

parts.words: Complaint of the motorist using too much petrol?
parts.note: complaint means illness, an old name for tuberculosis, which is also the word for fuel use by a car

explanation.surface: A driver grumbles about a thirsty car.
explanation.definitionFit: The old name for tuberculosis is also the term for the fuel a car burns.
